answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the signal schedule in the terrace ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ocean checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 146 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. That is 19 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
